Maya — thanks for the CSV and context, that helps. High level summary below; I attached a proposed burst matrix (Proposed_burst_matrix_v2.xlsx) with two packaging options.

Quick take:
- Baseline reserved: size to sustained steady-state (we recommend 40 GPUs based on your daily steady throughput in the CSV).
- Shoulder pool (ephemeral burst): a reserved-but-credit-backed pool you pay only when used. For your 2‑hour weekly spike we recommend a 20–30 GPU shoulder pool with dynamic pre-warm windows: pre-warm 20% of the shoulder pool 15 minutes before the window, then scale to full shoulder within 10 minutes of ramp.
- Credits model: shoulder credits are consumed when ephemeral GPUs are active; we can cap weekly credit usage and provide rollover for unused credits in quarter.
- Autoscale policy: aggressive up-scale (rapid allocation on traffic delta) + staggered pre-warm to avoid cold-model-shifts; conservative down-scale (cooldown 10m) to avoid oscillation. Include fallback to a cheaper quantized model variant when capacity is temporarily limited.

Next steps: Ben, Karthik — can you review the matrix and add technical constraints (GPU types, eviction tolerance) so we can share with Luminous procurement? Maya/Ethan — is 20–30 GPUs in the same ballpark you expected?

Thanks,
Priya
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Quick tech note from ops:
- GPU SKU: recommend A100-80GB equivalent for steady+burst. If they want lower unit cost we can run a mixed pool (steady on A100, shoulder on A30-like instances) but batching/kv-cache behavior will differ.
- Pre-warm: implement staged pre-warm — 20% 15m prior, 50% 7m prior, remaining 100% at start of ramp. That keeps cold-starting tails <200ms for most requests.
- Eviction & fallback: shoulder pool eviction should be FIFO based on session age + scoring; fallback to quantized L4 variant with slightly higher latency but 40% cost reduction if shoulder is saturated.
- Autoscale policy (concrete):
  * Scale-up threshold: sustained token/sec > 75% of current capacity for 60s -> trigger staging allocation.
  * Fast allocation path for shoulder: allocate in small slabs (4 GPUs) to avoid a single large placement failure.
  * Scale-down: cooldown 10m after traffic falls below 40% of baseline.

I'll attach a rough ops TCO: adding 25 GPUs of shoulder for 2h/week increases monthly spend by ~6% (with credit offsets) vs buying 24/7 reserved. Exact numbers in the attached matrix.

—Karthik
